column1: # gates/held-trees.tsv - THE REGISTER OF GATED-GREEN TREES THAT MUST NOT SHIP.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A "GATES GREEN" log says the gate suite passed over a bundle. It does NOT say that the
# tree shipped, or that it may. At 2026-10-01T00:31Z a run looking for a way out of a deadlock found a
# gated-green ancestor, ran every mechanical check this project provides, got four greens, and pushed a tree
# that #441 had deliberately held. All four checks were correct and none of them could see the hold:
#   git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main e765135          -> true
#   gates/verify-log.sh .../441-all.log '#441'                -> OK (47 suites, 3097 PASS, footer agrees)
#   git show e765135:app.js | md5sum                          -> a4df39c38222, the md5 that log's footer names
#   git show e765135 --stat                                   -> adds only the log file
# The only warning in existence was one sentence in a prose table cell on an unmerged branch: RUN-LOG.md:247 ON
# origin/claude/cool-noether-gccllp, reading "then stood down on two P0s from the adversarial pass" - which no
# tool reads and which main does not even carry. NAME THE TREE WHEN YOU CITE THAT LINE: both of #450's
# antagonists independently called this citation dangling, because line 247 OF MAIN is #437's job-counting rule,
# and the citation is exactly right on the tree where the sentence lives. One line number meaning two different
# things on two trees is not a footnote, it IS the defect.
# The push was reverted 17 minutes later by its own antagonist pass.
# Filed as jobs/a-gated-green-log-is-not-a-shippable-tree-2026-10-01 (P0, priority 11). This file is its fix.
# WHAT MAKES THIS A GUARD AND NOT A NOTE. It is keyed on things a LATER run can compute from the artefact it is
# holding, with no network and no tracker: the BUNDLE MD5 and the GATED SHA. gates.sh writes both into every log
# IT WRITES (the header line carries "md5 <hex>", the ref line carries "ref: HEAD <sha> | bundle md5 <hex>"), and
# `md5sum app.js` recovers the first from any tree on disk.
# BUT NOT INTO EVERY LOG THAT EXISTS, and the first draft of this paragraph said "every log", which antagonist B
# measured and disproved: the ref line arrived at #417, and 52 OF THE 81 COMMITTED GATELOGS (64%) carry no
# `ref: HEAD` line at all. verify-log.sh skips the sha comparison when it is absent, so ON MOST OF THIS
# PROJECT'S LOG CORPUS ONLY THE MD5 ARM FIRES. Said plainly because a guard's coverage is not a detail.
# gates/verify-log.sh reads this file BY DEFAULT and
# REFUSES a log naming a held bundle or a held sha. Nothing here is self-reported by the run that wants to push:
# the row is written by the run that HELD the tree, and read by a different run later. This project has recorded
# six separate defects whose single cause was that the check and the thing being checked were the same object;
# a `shippable` field written by the pushing run would have been the seventh.
# HOW TO WRITE A ROW. `gates/held.sh add <bundleMd5> <gatedSha> <#NNN> <reason...>` - or append by hand. Do it in
# THE SAME step as the stand-down, before the run ends, and commit it to MAIN rather than to the per-run branch:
# #441's own warning was lost precisely because it lived only on a branch that never merged, and a reverted
# commit takes its log with it. A row costs one line and survives a container being reclaimed.
# HOW TO CLEAR A ROW. Do NOT delete it. A tree does not become shippable by being forgotten. Change the first
# field to a `-` prefix (e.g. `-a4df39c38222`), which stops it matching, and append to the reason why it was
# cleared, with the sha that superseded it. The history is the useful part.
# A LIMIT OF THE FIRST TWO KEYS, MEASURED AT #450 RATHER THAN LEFT FOR SOMEONE TO FIND. `gates/build.sh:14`
# builds the stamp as `$N - $(TZ=America/New_York date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') ET` and embeds it with
# `--define:__BUILD__`, so THE BUNDLE MD5 CHANGES ON EVERY REBUILD IN A NEW MINUTE even from byte-identical
# source. Both bundleMd5 and gatedSha therefore identify an ARTEFACT, not a source tree: a run that REBUILDS a
# held source tree and commits it gets a fresh md5 and a fresh sha and matches neither. That is not the failure
# this register was written for - the 00:31Z push took an EXISTING gated-green tree, where both keys match - and
# a rebuild has to earn its own green suite anyway. But it is a real hole, so there is a seventh field:
# sourceMd5, `git show <sha>:chess.jsx | md5sum | cut -c1-12`, which is stamp-independent and survives a
# rebuild. `gates/held.sh check` compares it against the working tree's chess.jsx, and SO DOES `verify-log.sh`,
# via the sha on the log's own ref line. THIS PARAGRAPH FIRST SAID verify-log.sh "CANNOT use it and does not
# try", which antagonist A disproved in the same build: that script already reads the working tree for
# --this-bundle, and `git show <ref sha>:chess.jsx | md5sum` is reachable from the log alone. The false version
# is recorded because A's point was that a wrong sentence here is worse than the gap - it tells the next run not
# to bother. ITS OWN LIMIT, also A's: this is an EXACT-BLOB key, so it catches a straight carry-forward of the
# held source (four commits carry #441's chess.jsx byte-identical) and dies the moment one unrelated character
# changes. No key in this register tracks the DEFECT itself; that needs a predicate, and it is filed as
# jobs/a-held-row-should-carry-a-predicate-not-only-a-hash-2026-10-01.
# sourceMd5 is OPTIONAL - older rows and rows whose sha is unreachable may leave it `-`.
# FORMAT: tab-separated. bundleMd5 (first 12 hex, as gates.sh writes it) | gatedSha, COMMA-SEPARATED - every
# sha that names this tree, not only the gated one | build | heldAt
# (ISO-8601 UTC) | heldBy (runId) | reason (one sentence, the specific thing the suite could not see) |
# sourceMd5 (first 12 hex of chess.jsx at that sha, or `-`).
# bundleMd5

column6: HELD ON AN UPHELD ANTAGONIST VETO, AND THE SUITE NEVER FINISHED. The grading is arithmetically wrong in a way no gate in this suite can see: gradeDrillMove compares a DEPTH-2 score of the played move against a baseline that is the DEPTH-16 stored move, and loss=Math.min(1500,Math.max(0,...)) clamps a NEGATIVE difference to 0, so every move the shallow search happens to rate above the deep baseline is graded Best and told 'Nothing in the position beats it' - antagonist B measured 26 of 33 legal moves accepted in one quiet middlegame, 19 of them only because of that clamp. The mirror case is the same clamp at the ceiling: when the stored move is a mate, vBest is a mate score so every non-mating move reads loss 1500 and Blunder, measured 41 of 42 legal moves with 26 sharing one sentence - and drill cards are captured ONLY for Mistake, Blunder and Miss, so a decisive best move is the feature's normal case and not an edge. This is a WORSE version of the complaint the build was written to fix (Kunal: 'there can only be one best move'). Gate 52 is green at 20 PASS and cannot see any of it, because its fixture is one position with one hanging queen and three inputs. Separately two of the three sentences the feature is built around are unreachable by arithmetic against DRILL_MSG_MAXW=48 - 'Can you find it?' is selected 0 times out of 5 SANs - and my own unit control could not see it because it tested whether any candidate EXCEEDED the budget rather than which candidate was SELECTED. DO NOT SHIP THIS TREE. The grading needs a single instrument on both sides of the comparison before any of it is worth re-gating; see jobs/456-drill-grading-held-on-a-clamped-cross-instrument-loss-2026-10-02. (THE gatedSha IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG FOR ABOUT A MINUTE AND IS CORRECTED HERE BEFORE IT WAS COMMITTED: the first write padded the short hash 8dab924 into a 40-character string I INVENTED rather than reading git rev-parse. A register keyed on a sha is worthless if the sha is fabricated, and it would have failed silently - every later lookup would simply never match. Caught by re-reading my own command. [R18]) ### THREE MORE GROUNDS, FROM THE SECOND ANTAGONIST, EACH ALSO INVISIBLE TO THIS SUITE. (a) AN ACCEPT DESTROYS THE PLAYER'S OWN CARD, IRREVERSIBLY, ON A DEPTH-2 VERDICT: the useEffect keyed on puzSolved filters the card out of ct_mymistakes, and before #456 the only way to reach it was to play the engine's own move. Antagonist A measured 7 moves in one Sicilian middlegame accepted as Excellent at shallow loss 20-35 that a depth-4 ranking puts at 95-135cp. The old failure was "try again", annoying and recoverable; this one deletes captured data. (b) drillAcceptMsg IS NOT BUDGETED AT ALL, in the same 74px box this file budgets twice: measured against #426's own capacity figures for that box, the Excellent branch is 64-68 chars against 61 at 320x568 and the Brilliant branch 63-75, over at 320x568 by 2-14 and over KUNAL'S OWN 375x730 by up to 6 - and the Brilliant branch prefixes p.explain, which mistakeWhy has ALREADY packed to its own 52-char ceiling for this very box. No gate drives Excellent, Good or Brilliant, so C7 and C7b cannot see any of it. (c) C4, THE GATE'S OWN ANTI-GENERIC-STRING ASSERTION, IS FALSE IN THE COMMONEST CARD STATE: on a card whose stored move MATES - "you missed the mate" - vBest is a mate score so every non-mating move clamps to Blunder while bandAfter reads the position honestly, giving "Blunder: leaves you winning", a sentence that contradicts itself, and three different moves give 1 DISTINCT OF 3 after C4's own mask. AND THE BRILLIANT DRILL IS REACHED BY THE GRADING AND SHOULD NOT BE: a different move that gates Brilliant is told "That's your brilliant move. Nicely done." about a move that was not theirs. BOTH ANTAGONISTS ALSO RECORD THAT I REBUILT app.js TWICE WHILE THEY WERE MEASURING, which is the #441 mistake repeated and is why neither pass can be cited against one artefact without checking its timestamps.

The one-instrument baseline, the card-delete guard, the brilliant-drill exclusion and the mate sentence are all sound and worth keeping; what is owed is the two ladders and the accept band. A legacy 40-row account beside a month-walked account paints "Showing your 6 most recent months of play per account." over 70 rows, asserting the MONTH bound of an account that was never month-walked. That is a limit stated that did not bind - the #431/#432 class this very code block exists to remove - reintroduced in the one state the A10 table does not cover. Found by antagonist A at the diff door and RE-MEASURED by the build on this bundle before the veto was upheld. So the change trades one instance of the class for another, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a fix which opens the defect it closes elsewhere has to be visible. AND THE BUILD CERTIFIED THE REGRESSION IN ITS OWN GATE, which is the most useful thing in this row: having removed the inference it flipped A14a/A14b to expect the new output without asking whether the new output was right. That is A10c's own fault reproduced by the build written to fix A10c, in the same file, one block down. A14a is now rewritten to assert the REQUIREMENT - no limit may be asserted of every account while any account's bound is unknown - and is RED on this tree on purpose, so gates/regress/61-review-list-month-independence.js MUST NOT LAND ON MAIN until the union is fixed; a red assertion on main stops every later run emitting GATES GREEN. ANTAGONIST B RETURNED NO VETO, over 12 multi-account states, and measured that the store SELF-HEALS to ct_acctcap:months within 2.6s on the real returning-player path, so the population told less by the change is only the API-down or no-ct_ccuser legacy importer - where main's current sentence is itself false. B never drove A's fixture, and A never drove B's self-heal path, which is why the pair earned its budget. FIELD 7, THE SOURCE MD5, IS THE COMMITTED chess.jsx (36e0ae6b89cc) AND NOT THE ONE THE BUNDLE WAS BUILT FROM (075c38d643fb), deliberately: the bundle is the artefact both antagonists measured and was NOT rebuilt afterwards, while chess.jsx then took a COMMENT-ONLY correction to a premise that was false - it claimed ct_acctcap "arrives in #432 and #432 has never shipped", whereas measured at origin/main dcc5422 that grep reads 1, chess.jsx writes the key at :3749 and :3758, and main's bundle is stamped #452.
